name: Dorsal wrist arthroscopy portals
joint: radiocarpal, midcarpal, and distal radioulnar joints
corridor: Named dorsal portals in the intervals between extensor compartments, typically starting with the 3-4 viewing portal under finger-trap traction

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a hand table or traction tower, elbow flexed about 90°, and two digits in finger traps for distal distraction.

setup.text: Mark Lister tubercle, ECU, DRUJ, and planned portal sites before traction distorts landmarks. A 2.7-mm 30° arthroscope is the usual diagnostic scope. Limit traction; sources describe about 10 lb as a typical upper bound.

surface_landmarks.text: Lister tubercle locates the 3-4 portal about 1 cm distal in the soft spot between EPL and EDC. The 4-5 portal sits in line with the ring-finger metacarpal between EDC and EDM. 6R and 6U lie radial and ulnar to ECU. Midcarpal radial and ulnar portals sit about 1 cm distal to 3-4 and 4-5.

incision.text: Make a nick in skin only at the chosen portal, then spread with a hemostat to capsule before introducing a blunt trocar. Establish the 3-4 portal first, then create working and inflow portals under needle localization.

superficial_interval.text: Stay in the named extensor-compartment intervals. Protect EPL and EDC at 3-4, EDC and EDM at 4-5, and ECU at 6R/6U. Superficial sensory branches travel in the subcutaneous layer around the ulnar and radial portals.

deep_interval.text: Enter the radiocarpal joint at 3-4, then add 4-5 or 6R as the working portal. Use 6U commonly for inflow or ulnar-sided TFCC work. Inspect the midcarpal joint through MCR/MCU before calling the arthroscopy complete when instability is in question.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous sensory branches, extensor retinaculum and compartment intervals, dorsal capsule, then radiocarpal or midcarpal joint.

structures_encountered.text: EPL, EDC, EDM, ECU, dorsal capsule, scapholunate and lunotriquetral intervals, TFCC disc and foveal attachments, and the midcarpal articulations are encountered according to portal choice.

structures_at_risk.text: The dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve is closest to 6U and 6R. Superficial radial nerve and radial artery are closest to the 1-2 snuffbox portal. Extensor tendons are at risk at every dorsal portal. Articular cartilage is at risk from sharp trocar entry.

danger_zones.text: Cadaver mapping found essentially no free neurovascular margin at 1-2 and 6U. Avoid the 1-2 portal unless radial-styloid access is required, and spread bluntly just ulnar or radial to ECU rather than plunging beside it.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not lever cannulas against extensor tendons or drag instruments across the dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve at 6U. Keep traction modest to limit neuropraxia.

exposure.text: 3-4 is the primary viewing portal for the radiocarpal joint, including the TFCC from radial insertion to ulnar attachment. 4-5 or 6R is the usual working portal for probing and ulnar-sided TFCC work. Midcarpal portals complete assessment of carpal instability.

limitations.text: Standard dorsal portals give limited access to volar capsule and foveal footprint; some repairs need a dedicated foveal or volar portal. Diagnostic arthroscopy is not a substitute for a preoperative working diagnosis.

extensions.text: Add MCR and MCU for midcarpal inspection. A direct foveal portal about 1 cm proximal to 6U can expose the foveal footprint when deep TFCC fibers must be repaired.

indications.text: Use for unexplained mechanical wrist pain after failed nonoperative care, TFCC tears, interosseous ligament injury, chondral debridement, loose-body removal, ganglion excision, and arthroscopic assistance with selected intra-articular fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid when infection, advanced pancarpal arthritis, or local soft-tissue conditions make portal placement unsafe, or when a salvage reconstruction is already clearly indicated.

implant_implications.text: For peripheral TFCC repair, plan outside-in or all-inside sutures through 6R/6U without tethering ECU. Keep a peripheral rim if debriding a central tear so DRUJ stability is not lost.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Fluoroscopy is not required for portal creation but is used when arthroscopy assists fracture reduction or when confirming DRUJ alignment after TFCC repair.

closure.text: Remove cannulas, confirm tendon glide, and close portal skin loosely. Immobilize briefly as needed to allow portal healing and reduce synovial fistula risk.

complications.text: Complications include sensory neurapraxia (especially DSBUN at 6U and SRN at 1-2), extensor tendon injury, cartilage scuffing, stiffness, fluid extravasation, and portal fistula.

bailouts.text: If a portal cannot be entered safely, re-localize with a needle under arthroscopic vision from an established portal rather than enlarging blindly. Convert to open ulnar exposure if foveal repair cannot be completed arthroscopically.

procedure_applications.condition: Diagnostic or therapeutic wrist arthroscopy, including TFCC inspection, debridement, or peripheral repair

questions.question: Which portal is established first for diagnostic wrist arthroscopy?
questions.answer: The 3-4 portal, about 1 cm distal to Lister tubercle between EPL and EDC.

questions.question: Which nerve is most at risk at the 6U portal?
questions.answer: The dorsal sensory branch of the ulnar nerve.

questions.question: Which portal is typically used as the working portal for TFCC instrumentation?
